acceptance: roadmap/debt.yaml (schema shipped with init project and refresh-schemas) holds entries {id, title, found_in (node id or free text), paths, severity, status open|planned|closed, node (when planned)}; specy-road debt add|list|close manage it without hand edits
specy-road debt plan <id> --under <PARENT> creates the leaf through add-node, links it, and marks the entry planned; closing the leaf (finish-this-task) closes the entry
roadmap-context.md lists open debt by severity (at most 10 lines); validate warns on an entry whose linked node no longer exists
nodes.title: A tracked tech-debt ledger that planning can turn into leaves

acceptance: specy-road models stats prints per reviewer model, over the last N recorded reviews (default 50): reviews, block rate, approvals overturned (another model blocked the same commit and the leaf then changed), mean probes per approve (M14.5 when present) and mean commands_rerun lines, from local review records and the tracked Review-tally trailers M12.4.1 adds

With policy.evidence_scoring on (default off), orchestrate plan lowers a reviewer's score when its overturned-approval rate exceeds a policy threshold and says so in the plan; off leaves plans unchanged; a test pins both
Out of scope: the digest (per-area scores are M12.4.1) and changing the roster automatically
nodes.title: Per-model review evidence: block rate and overturned approvals feed orchestrate plan

acceptance: specy-road worktree cleanup <ID>, run from the main checkout after finish-this-task lands the leaf, first moves leaf-local hand-off files (work/reviews/<ID>/** in the leaf's worktree, including history/ copies and RUN-* logs) into the shared hand-off directory (reviews_root), never overwriting a different file (it keeps both, the moved one with a suffix); then terminates the leaf's worker if one is idle and removes the worktree; a test puts a review history file only in the leaf worktree's ignored work/reviews/<ID>/history/ and asserts it exists in the main checkout's hand-off dir after cleanup and the worktree is gone

cleanup refuses, removes nothing and prints one line per reason when the worktree has commits not on the integration branch, uncommitted changes or untracked files git does not ignore, or ignored files outside a known-regenerable list (__pycache__ and tool caches, node_modules, work/prompt-*.md, work/brief-*.md, work/.on-complete-*.yaml, .specyrd/cache/) once hand-off files are moved; reuses worktree_prune.plan_prune (including M14.3's foreign-worktree refusal) and worker terminate; a test per refusal

specy-road worktree sweep [--dry-run] lists every linked worktree (wherever it lives, e.g. under .claude/worktrees/ or a temp dir) whose branch or detached HEAD is contained in the integration branch, with no registry claim (so never a claimed or deferred leaf's), no live or resumable worker, no live session, and nothing unsaved by the cleanup rules; it removes each (moving hand-off files first) or with --dry-run only reports; output is one line per worktree: removed, would remove, or kept with the reason; it uses M14.2's live-leaf rules rather than a copy; a test with a claimed, a live-session, a dirty and a removable worktree pins the four lines

grind-session runs cleanup after each leaf it lands, and policy.worktree_sweep (off by default; between_leaves) makes it run sweep between leaves; the specyrd-orchestrate command tells the coordinator to run worktree cleanup <ID> after finish and worktree sweep --dry-run at the start of a session; docs/orchestration-chores.md documents both

Out of scope: deleting remote branches (never); local branch deletion only with --delete-local-branch, only for a branch the integration branch contains; cleaning the main checkout's work/ files (finish-this-task's cleanup already owns those)

worktree cleanup and sweep also end the session presence records tied to the removed worktree or its deleted branch (the leaf's worker, reviewer and session entries), so session list shows none for a landed leaf; a test with a leftover reviewer and session record asserts both are gone after cleanup

sweep removes a pickup-created worktree whose branch the integration branch contains (the reported case: it stayed after finish, and branch pruning skipped its branch as '(worktree)'), and after removal the branch is no longer skipped; a test covers it

docs/orchestration-chores.md warns that gh pr merge --delete-branch can remove a leaf's branch while its worktree still holds uncommitted or ignored hand-off files, and says to run worktree cleanup <ID> (which saves hand-off files first) before deleting the branch
nodes.title: The orchestrator cleans up landed leaves and stale worktrees automatically, saving hand-off files first

acceptance: `grind-session --workers N` (N >= 1; the default 1 keeps today's one-leaf loop) runs a tick loop that keeps up to N live workers: each tick it claims ready, unclaimed, unheld leaves in pickup order into their own worktrees (as `do-next-available-task --worktree` does) and runs `worker delegate` with orchestrate assign's executor; a leaf is skipped while one of its zones overlaps a live claim's zones under the shared-zone rule in shared_zones.py; `policy.max_workers_per_model` (a map of roster id to integer >= 1 in orchestration.schema.json) caps live workers per model at every `worker delegate`, whose refusal names the model and its cap

Each tick, in this order: a claim whose gate is met at its branch tip is landed with finish-this-task (M16.14's land checks) whether or not a worker record still exists; a claim whose READY names its branch tip, with a clean post-run check and no review record at that commit, is handed to `review run` (M18.24); a claim with no live worker, no READY and no worker record is delegated again under the same caps

Held leaves (one id per line in the gitignored work/grind-hold.txt, `#` starts a reason, re-read every tick) are never claimed, messaged, reviewed or landed, and their claims hold no zones; with `grind.release_zones_in_review: true` (git-workflow.schema.json, default false) a claim whose READY names its tip stops holding its zones; while the integration checkout has uncommitted tracked changes the loop takes no git action and emits one `waiting_dirty_checkout` event

Every action is one JSON line in the grind event log (delegated, review_started, landed, held_skip, waiting_dirty_checkout, cap_reached naming the model); the schedule is set by flags and git-workflow.yaml only, never by an environment variable; after a restart the loop re-evaluates every claim from the M16.15 snapshot and re-runs an interrupted landing

Tests with a stub harness and no network: two leaves sharing a zone are delegated one after the other and two disjoint leaves together; a per-model cap of 1 holds the second leaf; a held leaf is skipped; a met gate with no worker record lands; a dirty checkout waits; `--workers 1` gives the M16.19 grind table's rows unchanged. Out of scope: automatic fix rounds (M18.21), supervision (M18.22), account pools (M18.23)
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +350, tests about +300
nodes.title: Unattended grind loop: several workers at once, zone-overlap scheduling, per-model caps, review hand-off and landing when the gate is met

acceptance: The M18.20 loop writes work/grind-heartbeat.json each tick (pid, tick time, --workers); `doctor` and `grind-session --status` read it with the M16.15 snapshot, the grind event log and the review run records, and report each row of one table in new specy_road/orchestration/supervision.py: loop pid gone or heartbeat older than three ticks; a worker in state failed with no later event on its leaf; a running worker with no event for 45 minutes; a completed or idle worker whose leaf has no review running, no fix round and no landing for 15 minutes; review runs waiting for a slot with none running for 15 minutes; a ready, unclaimed, unheld leaf not delegated for 30 minutes, with the reason (the overlapping claim and zone, or the capped model); uncommitted tracked changes in the integration checkout for 5 minutes

Each problem is one line naming the leaf or worker, its age and the next command; `--json` lists them with the row id; the thresholds are named constants in that table and docs/orchestration.md lists them; supervision rows are doctor warnings, so doctor's exit codes are unchanged
The report is read-only: it restarts, re-sends and terminates nothing; docs/grind-session.md shows restarting a dead loop from the user's own supervisor (a cron or systemd example)
Tests: one fixture per table row and one healthy fixture with no rows, all with a fixed clock (no sleeps)
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +200, tests about +200
nodes.title: doctor reports a stalled orchestration: a silent loop, failed or stalled workers, idle leaves, a stuck review queue, undelegated ready leaves and a dirty checkout

acceptance: `specy-road review run <NODE_ID>` (new specy_road/review_run.py, registered from review_delegate's parser as M18.10's `review rca` is, so review_cli gains no subcommand code) builds the packet for the branch tip, refuses before any launch on a trial-merge conflict with the integration branch (the generated roadmap files finish resolves excepted) or on M18.9's zone check, then runs `review delegate` for each reviewer the policy requires that has no record at the tip, in roster order; with `policy.review_order: sequential` (orchestration.schema.json, default parallel) the next reviewer starts only after the previous one approves, and a block ends the run

`policy.max_concurrent_reviews` (integer >= 1, orchestration.schema.json, default no cap) caps reviewer launches across processes in one checkout with slot files under work/reviews/.slots/ holding the owner's pid (a slot whose pid is gone is reclaimed); a run waits for a slot in arrival order, `--no-wait` exits 3 printing `queued: no review slot`; a second `review run` for a leaf that already has one running exits 0 at once, printing the running run's pid, and leaves its slot and markers alone

When `review record` refuses a reviewer's final answer (outcome rerun from a record refusal, not a capacity error), `review delegate` resumes the same session once with the refusal text (the offending lines and rule M15.17 prints) and asks for a corrected final answer; a second refusal is final; `--refusal-retries 0` turns it off; the RUN record lists both attempts

Tests with a stub reviewer and no network: sequential order stops after a block; parallel order runs both; a cap of 1 makes a second leaf wait; a stale slot is reclaimed; a duplicate run returns at once; a refused answer then a valid one files one record; two refusals end incomplete
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +250, tests about +250
nodes.title: review run: the required reviewers in order for one leaf, a concurrency cap across leaves, and one retry on a refused record

acceptance: `edit-node` on a leaf with a registry claim that changes touch_zones or acceptance refuses without `--reason <text>`; with it, the same write appends `- <date> <fields changed>: <reason>` under `## Amendments` in the leaf's planning sheet (adding the heading when missing); on an unclaimed leaf edit-node behaves as today and records the line only when `--reason` is given

`--set-acceptance-line N=<text>` replaces and `--append-acceptance-line N=<text>` extends acceptance line N (1-based) and leaves the other lines unchanged; an index out of range is refused, writing nothing

Run from the integration checkout on a claimed leaf with a linked worktree, edit-node also applies the change in that worktree and commits it on the leaf branch (`roadmap(<ID>): amend <fields> (<reason>)`); it refuses, writing nothing in either tree, while that worktree has uncommitted changes or the leaf's worker is running

After a zone amendment, the worker's post-run out-of-zone findings for paths the new zones cover are cleared and a worker event (worker-event.schema.json) records the clearing; approvals at earlier commits are stale as for any new commit, and handoff status names the amendment line as the reason a review is needed

Tests: a claimed leaf without --reason is refused; with it, the sheet line and the branch commit exist; a dirty worktree refuses with both trees unchanged; a covered out-of-zone finding is cleared and an uncovered one kept; one-line acceptance edits by index, and an out-of-range index refused
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +150, tests about +160
nodes.title: Amending a claimed leaf's touch zones or one acceptance line records the reason, commits on the leaf branch and re-arms its review
